transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Elena, Jonah, Samir, Maya, Aaron, Marissa, Sonia, Daniel
Links shared: confluence/infra/kms-rotation (placeholder), drive/finance/dec-expense.xlsx

Summary: quick sync to finalize KMS rotation plan (prod keys), align finance on expense rationalization and confirm December patch window / maintenance freeze. Cross-functional: IT, Security, Finance, Procurement.

[00:00] Priya: okay everyone, thanks for joining the monthly ops sync, I know this is packed — main things: key rotation, cost clean-up, and patch window. We'll go in that order and leave time for Qs.
[00:24] Aaron: sounds good, I'm mostly on the expense side, want to hear timing because finance needs to cut any invoices before freeze.
[00:32] Elena: quick note — we already have a partial runbook for KMS rotation in confluence but it's stale, and we haven't tested prod fallback in isolation.
[00:42] Samir: right, plus we need to ensure audit logs and HSM / KMS key policy changes are captured for SOC2 — last time some of the log buckets were missing retention tags.
[00:54] Jonah: and from infra, rotating keys will touch token-service and any infra clients using the envelope keys; we need to snapshot and have a rollback plan. Snapshotting is fast but some of the stateful services may have in-memory caches.
[01:10] Marissa: on costs — we ran a quick query on reserved GPU pools and there's about 18% underutilized DEDICATED capacity on east-1. We think some of that can be shifted or downsized.
[01:22] Sonia: also the AP queue has some POs that haven't matched to invoices, that needs procurement help.

[03:05] Priya: ok, Elena, can you walk us through the runbook gaps? 
[03:16] Elena: sure. Step 1: identify aliases for current key (there's the prod-kms-v2 and an older prod-master, sometimes clients point to the alias not key id which is good), Step 2: create new key in same region, set policy, test with dev tokens, Step 3: rotate alias to new key, Step 4: deprecate old key after 30d. 
[03:45] Elena: missing things: a) precise rollback commands, b) verification script for every infra client (we have a rough script but it misses some internal tooling), c) coordination window so finance/backup/partners know when to expect possible short auth failures.
[04:06] Priya: great. Jonah, what's the time estimate for snapshot + smoke test?
[04:12] Jonah: snapshot of token-service AMI and db point-in-time is 18-25 minutes, restore test on a small instance about 10-12, full smoke test for auth flows 20-30 but can run parallel with clients. Conservatively 1.5 hours with warm-up.
[04:40] Aaron: that's fine but finance can't have billback and invoice export jobs running during that window, they said they need a quiet window.
[04:49] Marissa: yeah, ideally not during EOD close — we suggested 12/11 or 12/12 but open to other slots.

[06:05] Samir: security concerns — KMS rotation requires re-signing service tokens and we must keep key arn references consistent. Also log pipelines must be captured: CloudTrail, KMS CloudTrail events, and the S3 buckets must have encryption turned on. I saw a mis-sized retention on logs in staging.
[06:27] Elena: noted, I'll add verification steps for CloudTrail event delivery. Also will ensure S3 retention tags.

[07:00] Maya: one thing we hit last audit — some artifact owners were undefined for certain encryption processes, so Samir if you can map artifact->owner that helps.
[07:12] Samir: yes I'll take that.

[08:20] Daniel: procurement — if you rotate keys will any vendor integrations break? Payment gateways? We need a compatibility check with external vendors.
[08:29] Jonah: good catch, we have oauth tokens for a couple vendors that use envelope encryption. We'll enumerates vendor clients and run tests.

[09:02] Elena: also we need to avoid rotation during payroll or billing cycles. I'll propose three windows: 12/06 02:00-04:00 UTC (off-peak), 12/11 10:00-12:00 UTC (mid-morning), 12/12 22:00-00:00 UTC (low activity).
[09:30] Aaron: finance prefers 12/11 morning. 12/06 might be too soon for AP.
[09:40] Marissa: can we do a short freeze for exports 30 min before and after? That would mitigate mismatches.

[11:20] Priya: moving on — expense rationalization. Marissa, walk us through the top line.
[11:28] Marissa: yes. I pivoted the sheet to show top 10 cost drivers: GPU reserved pools, cepheus storage tier (naming obf), ci/cd runner spend (gitlab), and idle dedicated nodes. The quick wins: reclaim unused reserved nodes (50% usage threshold), tag enforcement (about 17% untagged resources), and shutting down pre-prod clusters overnight.
[11:50] Sonia: AP sees many small subscriptions that roll monthly — we should consolidate vendor accounts and renegotiate.
[12:02] Aaron: also look at license seats for developer tools — some teams have duplicate paid accounts.

[13:40] Jonah: technical note: shutting pre-prod clusters overnight requires automation to safely drain pods and preserve DB caches. We'll need a runbook for grace period and restart schedule.
[13:55] Elena: can add cron-scheduler in cluster-manager and implement a short 'grace-shutdown' hook.

[15:10] Samir: remember quantization tests or model infra might be sensitive to cold-start — we should whitelist any endpoints with SLAs from auto-shutdown.
[15:24] Marissa: will list those endpoints and owners in the sheet.

[17:00] Daniel: procurement process improvements — PO matching fails due to missing cost center tags. If we enforce tags on creation we can reduce manual AP work.
[17:12] Marissa: agreed, we'll add tagging required policy and a short training doc for teams.

[19:05] Priya: SOC2 audit prep quick hit — Samir, which artifacts are outstanding?
[19:12] Samir: off the top: key rotation logs, access review evidence for infra, vendor risk assessments for payments, and incident response playbook sign-offs. Some are in confluence but need official owners.
[19:28] Maya: I can help format the artifact checklist for auditors and include owners and location links.

[21:40] Priya: ok let's surface risks: any blockers to rotation?
[21:48] Jonah: vendor tests pending — I need 48 hours to run them once windows are chosen.
[21:54] Daniel: procurement needs 24 hours notice before we block payment jobs.
[22:00] Marissa: finance will need final date by EOD Monday to process cutoffs.

[24:05] Priya: decision point — pick the window. Does 12/11 10:00-12:00 UTC work?
[24:12] Aaron: yes from finance side.
[24:15] Elena: I can accept that.
[24:18] Jonah: will schedule vendor tests for 12/09-12/10.
[24:24] Samir: Security will do a dry-run against staging on 12/07.

[26:00] (crosstalk) Sonia: and AP will stop batch exports 30 min prior.
[26:10] Priya: good — so agreed: 12/11 10-12 UTC. Runbook draft due 12/10. Dry-run and vendor tests scheduled.

[28:40] Priya: final area — December patch window and freeze. Ops proposed a freeze 12/18-12/28 for major deployments, micro-patches allowed if security critical. Thoughts?
[28:53] Aaron: finance likes a freeze but needs a one-time patch for billing on 12/20 if necessary.
[29:05] Jonah: we should allow scheduled emergency patches with 2 approvers and on-call notified.
[29:12] Samir: security agrees, but we want a firm definition of "security critical" and an approval SLA.
[29:20] Maya: I'll draft a one-paragraph definition and approval flow and post to confluence.

[31:50] Priya: any open Qs on procurement invoices? Daniel?
[31:58] Daniel: I'll escalate the 12 stale POs; may reassign to vendor managers by 12/09.

[33:10] Marissa: one more ask — can infra provide a quick token where finance can re-run exports while rotation is in progress in case of failures?
[33:22] Jonah: we can provide temporary backup credentials but they'd be short-lived and must be rotated post-use. We'll document the flow.

[35:00] (brief pause)
[35:20] Priya: ok recap: 1) KMS rotation window 12/11 10-12 UTC, runbook due 12/10 (Elena), dry-run 12/07 (Samir), vendor tests 12/09-10 (Jonah). 2) Expense rationalization: Marissa to share sheet 12/08; infra to propose auto-shutdown runbook. 3) Patch freeze 12/18-12/28 with emergency patch process (Maya to draft). 4) AP/Procurement action on invoices by 12/09.
[35:55] Aaron: confirm I'll get final date by Monday EOD.
[36:02] Priya: links — I'll post confluence runbook link and a drive sheet.

[37:10] (transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings; some speaker labels generic)
[37:30] Marissa: I'll circulate the expense heatmap after the call.
[37:40] Sonia: AP will pause exports 30 min before the rotation.

[40:00] Priya: anything else?
[40:05] Samir: one small ask — make sure KMS CloudTrail log bucket has proper lifecycle and encryption. I'll check and send remediation steps.
[40:20] Elena: noted.

[42:10] Priya: if no other items we can close. Thanks all.
[42:15] (some goodbyes)

End of transcript.

Action items repeated in transcript for clarity.

Shared artifacts: drive/finance/dec-expense.xlsx (placeholder), confluence/infra/kms-rotation-runbook-draft (placeholder), confluence/ops/patch-freeze-policy (placeholder).

All stakeholders agreed on a date; runbook and dry-run schedules set
Key risk: vendor integration tests required to avoid payment failures
